law_name: Rigorous implementation of the Dublin asylum framework and asylum/foreign nationals policy
description: As Head of the Federal Department of Justice and Police, pursued strict implementation of the Dublin Agreement and intensified negotiations with third states on the readmission of asylum seekers.
significance: Continued Switzerland's restrictive asylum-enforcement line; a defining theme of her tenure as Justice Minister.

law_name: Revision of the Weapons Act (implementation of the EU firearms directive / Schengen)
description: Tightening of Swiss weapons law to align with the revised EU firearms directive, defended by her department and approved in a popular vote in May 2019.
significance: Secured Switzerland's continued participation in Schengen/Dublin by adopting the EU firearms rules despite a referendum challenge.

law_name: Extension of the anti-racism criminal norm to sexual orientation
description: Extension of the criminal provision against discrimination to cover discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation, approved in a popular vote in February 2020.
significance: Extended legal protection against discrimination to LGBT people.

law_name: Marriage for All (Ehe für alle) - Civil Code amendment
description: Amendment to the Civil Code opening civil marriage to same-sex couples, with adoption rights and access to sperm donation for female couples. Approved by 64.1% of voters on 26 September 2021 and in force from 1 July 2022. As Justice Minister, Keller-Sutter represented the government position in favour.
significance: Landmark equality reform; Keller-Sutter said it ended existing inequalities of treatment.

law_name: Federal Act on Police Measures to Combat Terrorism (PMT)
description: Law expanding preventive police measures against terrorism, defended by her department and approved in a popular vote in June 2021. Its broad definition of terrorism drew criticism, including from the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.
significance: Significantly expanded preventive police powers; controversial on human-rights grounds.

law_name: Emergency measures for the takeover of Credit Suisse by UBS (March 2023)
description: As Finance Minister, led the federal response to the collapse of Credit Suisse. On 19 March 2023 the Federal Council adopted, partly under emergency law (Notrecht), a package including federal guarantees and liquidity assistance enabling UBS to take over Credit Suisse. The government later committed to converting the emergency measures into ordinary law and reviewing too-big-to-fail rules.
significance: One of the largest banking rescues in Swiss history; reshaped the Swiss banking landscape and the too-big-to-fail debate.

law_name: Implementation of the OECD/G20 minimum tax (15%) - constitutional amendment
description: Constitutional amendment to implement the OECD/G20 minimum taxation of 15% for large internationally active corporate groups (annual revenue above EUR 750 million). Championed by Keller-Sutter as Finance Minister and approved by voters and the cantons on 18 June 2023.
significance: Aligned Switzerland with the international minimum-tax regime while seeking to retain tax revenue domestically.
